mechanisms.description: An order whose only command revokes, vacates, amends or restores is performed when it issues; it is spent on issue as a command, and its effect is evidence about the order it acts on.

Relinquishment under the Act of July 5, 1884: the President places reservation lands found useless for military purposes under the Secretary of the Interior for disposal. The order ends the military reservation over the lands it names.

A later executive order that revokes, vacates, rescinds or supersedes the member by number or date, or relinquishes all of the member's lands, ends it. Version 1 uses 25 such orders whose texts are held (23 are members of this family; EO 7320 and EO 9293 are not).

Philippine independence: surrender of all U.S. reservations by Proclamation 2695 on July 4, 1946 under sec. 10(a) of the 1934 Act, and of all remaining rights except base use by agreement under the Treaty of General Relations on October 22, 1946.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: interval from the order date to 1946-10-22

mechanisms.description: End of the Canal Zone: the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979, Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction, and later U.S. use of military areas rested on the Treaty and its Article IV implementing agreement; the Treaty terminated December 31, 1999.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: interval from the order date to 1979-10-01

mechanisms.description: Hawaii Admission Act sec. 5(c) and 5(e): lands set aside by executive order remained U.S. property at statehood; lands found no longer needed within five years were conveyed to the State. A lead for each Hawaii tract.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: none for the class; conveyance date per tract

mechanisms.description: FLPMA sec. 701(c) savings and sec. 704(a) repeal of withdrawal authority (1976); the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. These keep existing reservations in force until modified and are never an end.

sources.citation: Philippine Independence Act (Tydings-McDuffie Act), Act of Mar. 24, 1934, ch. 84, secs. 5 and 10, 48 Stat. 456, 459, 463
sources.title: Philippine Independence Act
sources.pin: including all military and other reservations
sources.establishes: Section 10(a) directed the President, on the July 4 after ten years of the Commonwealth, to withdraw and surrender all U.S. possession, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the Philippine Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; section 10(b) left naval reservations and fueling stations 'in its present status' pending negotiation.

sources.citation: Proclamation No. 2695, Independence of the Philippines, July 4, 1946, 60 Stat. 1352, 1353
sources.title: Proclamation 2695
sources.pin: hereby withdraws and surrenders
sources.establishes: On July 4, 1946, acting under the 1934 Act and 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', the President withdrew and surrendered all U.S. rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the territory and people of the Philippines.

sources.citation: Treaty of General Relations between the United States and the Republic of the Philippines, signed July 4, 1946, art. I, 61 Stat. 1174 (ratifications exchanged and in force Oct. 22, 1946)
sources.title: Treaty of General Relations (Treaty of Manila) 1946
sources.pin: except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases
sources.establishes: Article I (read on the web, not held) withdraws and surrenders all U.S. rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control or sovereignty over the Philippine Islands, except the use of such bases as the United States may by agreement with the Republic deem necessary to retain; the treaty entered into force on October 22, 1946, so any base withheld under the 1944 joint resolution or kept 'in its present status' under section 10(b) was thereafter used under agreement, not under the reserving executive order.

sources.citation: Joint Resolution of June 29, 1944, ch. 322, sec. 2, 58 Stat. 626 (22 U.S.C. 1392)
sources.title: Philippine bases joint resolution
sources.pin: withhold or to acquire and to retain such bases
sources.establishes: Authorized the President, after negotiation, to withhold or acquire and retain bases in the Philippines in addition to those provided for by the 1934 Act; it explains why some Army reservations were not surrendered on July 4, 1946 (read on the web through 22 U.S.C. 1392, not held).

sources.citation: Panama Canal Act of 1979, Pub. L. 96-70, secs. 3(b)(1), 1504 and 3304, 93 Stat. 452, 455, 488, 500
sources.title: Panama Canal Act of 1979
sources.pin: shall be deemed to refer to the areas and
sources.establishes: From the date the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force (sec. 3304), 'Canal Zone' in U.S. law is deemed to refer to the areas and installations in the Republic of Panama made available to the United States under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)); the Zone as U.S.-controlled territory in which the President set apart reservations ceased on that date.

sources.citation: Panama Canal Treaty, signed Sept. 7, 1977, arts. II, IV, XI, 33 U.S.T. 39, T.I.A.S. No. 10030, 1280 U.N.T.S. 3 (No. 21086); in force Oct. 1, 1979
sources.title: Panama Canal Treaty of 1977
sources.pin: shall reassume plenary jurisdiction over the former Canal Zone
sources.establishes: The Treaty came into force on October 1, 1979; on entry into force it terminated and superseded the Isthmian Canal Convention of 1903 (art. I(1)(a)) and Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction over the former Canal Zone on entry into force; U.S. military use of defense sites thereafter rested on the separate Agreement in Implementation of Article IV; the Treaty terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (read on the web in the UNTS copy, not held).

sources.citation: Act of July 5, 1884, ch. 214, sec. 1, 23 Stat. 103
sources.title: Abandoned Military Reservations Act
sources.pin: to be placed under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition
sources.establishes: When the President finds the lands of a military reservation, or any portion, useless for military purposes, he shall cause them to be placed under the control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition under the Act (read on the web, not held); an order made under it relinquishes the military reservation over the lands it names.

sources.citation: Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-579, secs. 701(c) and 704(a), 90 Stat. 2743, 2786, 2792
sources.title: FLPMA
sources.pin: in effect as of the date of approval of this Act shall remain in full
sources.establishes: Section 704(a) repealed, from October 21, 1976, the President's implied withdrawal authority and the withdrawal sections of the Pickett Act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847); section 701(c) kept all withdrawals and reservations then in effect in full force until modified under FLPMA or other law. This is a continuity point, never an end.

sources.title: Engle Act
sources.pin: on and after February 28, 1958 the provisions hereof shall apply
sources.establishes: Requires an Act of Congress for defense withdrawals of more than 5,000 acres made on and after February 28, 1958 (read on the web through 43 U.S.C. 155, not held); it is prospective and neither ends nor confirms an earlier executive-order reservation.

sources.citation: Hawaii Admission Act, Pub. L. 86-3, sec. 5(c) and 5(e), 73 Stat. 4, 5-6 (1959)
sources.title: Hawaii Admission Act
sources.pin: shall remain the property of the United States subject only to the limitations, if any, imposed
sources.establishes: Lands set aside for federal use by Act, proclamation or executive order on the date of admission remained U.S. property (sec. 5(c)); each agency was to report within five years, and land the President found no longer needed was to be conveyed to the State (sec. 5(e)) (read on the web, not held). It is a lead for each Hawaii reservation, not an end or a continuation of any one order.

sources.title: Military Bases Agreement 1947
sources.establishes: Not read in full. Needed only if the owner wants to test the doctrine's position that U.S. use of retained Philippine bases after 1946 rested on this agreement rather than on the reserving executive orders.

lead.basis: By its own terms the order performs one act: it takes the named lands out of a military or naval reservation (restoring them, relinquishing them to a territorial or Philippine government, or placing them under the Interior Department for disposal under the Act of July 5, 1884). The act was complete when the order issued; later disposal of the lands proceeds under the statute and the land laws, not under a continuing command of the order.

gaps: A later order could vacate a transfer to the Interior Department before disposal (EO 1011, EO 2377, EO 2563 and EO 636 did so for EO 803, EO 1422, EO 1279 and EO 372-B); a vacated transfer is ended by the vacating order (branches C09, C16, C23, C24), and the doctrine detects vacatur only where the vacating order is a member of this family.
Regex screens on the text decide that no reversion, retained right, redefinition or re-reservation is present; scan-OCR texts may hide such a clause.

procedure.description: Philippine reservations: orders that reserve, enlarge, redefine or transfer military or naval reservations in the Philippine Islands (any order of this family located there that the earlier branches did not decide).

not.summary_regex: C\. ?Z\.|Canal Zone|Balboa|Col[oó]n Naval|Coco Solo|Fort Amador|Fort Randolph|France Field|Quarry Heights|Corozal|Fort Clayton|Fort Sherman|Paitilla|Cerro Tigre|Corundu|Republic of Panama

not.any_regex: Four-hour work ?day|Civil ?Service Rules|Duties of the United States Marine Corps|Seizure of German vessels|Foreign vessels ?prohibited|\"military camps,\"|imprisonment of Coast Guard prisoners

lead.basis: Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act (48 Stat. 463) required the surrender on July 4, 1946 of all U.S. possession, control and sovereignty over the Islands 'including all military and other reservations', and Proclamation 2695 made that surrender; naval reservations, and bases withheld under the 1944 joint resolution, passed under Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946), which surrendered all remaining U.S. rights except the use of bases by agreement. After that date no U.S. reservation of Philippine land by executive order could operate; any later U.S. use of a base rested on the 1947 Military Bases Agreement.

date_rule.basis: ended no later than the Treaty of General Relations' entry into force; July 4, 1946 for reservations surrendered by Proclamation 2695; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) is read on the web only; acquire it.

If the owner treats U.S. use of a retained base under the 1947 Military Bases Agreement as a continuation of the reserving order, the upper bound moves to that base's turnover (all before the cutoff); the doctrine takes the agreement as a new basis, as the Jacquard L6 lot card does.
The place screen reads the title, the WPA summary and the held text; a scan that runs into a neighbouring Philippine order can pull in a member located elsewhere.

lead.basis: The President set these reservations apart within the Canal Zone, or on adjacent lands whose use the 1903 Isthmian Canal Convention granted. When the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979, it terminated and superseded the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)(a)) and Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone (art. XI), and the Panama Canal Act of 1979 (sec. 3(b)(1)) thereafter treats 'Canal Zone' as the areas in the Republic of Panama made available to the United States under the Treaty. Any later U.S. military use rested on the Treaty and its Article IV implementing agreement, and the Treaty terminated at noon on December 31, 1999.

date_rule.basis: ended no later than the Panama Canal Treaty's entry into force; earlier if a later order superseded or rescinded it

gaps: The Panama Canal Treaty (UNTS 1280, No. 21086) is read on the web only; acquire it.

If the owner treats U.S. use of a defense site under the Article IV agreement as a continuation of the reserving order, the upper bound moves to 1999-12-31 (Treaty termination), still before the cutoff.

procedure.description: Hawaii reservations: orders that reserve, enlarge or redefine military or naval reservations in Hawaii.

not.any_regex: Four-hour work ?day|Civil ?Service Rules|Duties of the United States Marine Corps|Seizure of German vessels|Foreign vessels ?prohibited|\"military camps,\"|imprisonment of Coast Guard prisoners

lead.basis: Many of these reservations (for example Fort Shafter, Fort DeRussy, Fort Ruger, Schofield-area and Pearl Harbor tracts) may still be federal land. Section 5(c) of the Hawaii Admission Act kept lands set aside by executive order as U.S. property, and section 5(e) required conveyance to the State of lands found no longer needed; neither fixes the status of any one order.

gaps: Current federal real property or Army/Navy installation records for each tract, and section 5(e) conveyance records, would decide yes or no; acquire the Hawaii Admission Act text.

procedure.description: Alaska reservations: orders that reserve, enlarge or modify military or naval reservations, Signal Corps stations or radio stations in Alaska.

not.any_regex: Four-hour work ?day|Civil ?Service Rules|Duties of the United States Marine Corps|Seizure of German vessels|Foreign vessels ?prohibited|\"military camps,\"|imprisonment of Coast Guard prisoners

lead.basis: Many Alaska reservations were later placed under the Interior Department by blanket orders (for example EO 4131 of 1925 and EO 7127 of 1935, both members), often with exceptions for cemeteries, Signal Corps tracts or Alaska Road Commission sites; others passed through statehood selections, ANCSA conveyances or Public Land Orders. Which instrument ended a given reservation is a tract question.

gaps: Match each reservation's name and the orders' recitals to the blanket relinquishments (EO 4131, EO 7127, EO 7049) and to BLM Alaska Public Land Order records; a whole-reservation match is an ACT end.

procedure.description: Puerto Rico reservations: orders that reserve, transfer or modify naval or military lands in Puerto Rico.

not.any_regex: Four-hour work ?day|Civil ?Service Rules|Duties of the United States Marine Corps|Seizure of German vessels|Foreign vessels ?prohibited|\"military camps,\"|imprisonment of Coast Guard prisoners

lead.basis: Puerto Rico remains a U.S. territory; no class-wide event ended these reservations. Each depends on later transfers to the insular government or federal disposal.

gaps: Later executive orders, statutes or deeds transferring the named lands, or current federal property records.

procedure.description: Continental reservations: orders that reserve, enlarge, redefine or transfer military or naval reservations, target and rifle ranges (including Pickett Act withdrawals for the National Guard), or lands for another department's use in the States.

not.any_regex: Four-hour work ?day|Civil ?Service Rules|Duties of the United States Marine Corps|Seizure of German vessels|Foreign vessels ?prohibited|\"military camps,\"|imprisonment of Coast Guard prisoners

lead.basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example Fort Sill, Fort Bliss ranges) may still be military land.

gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.
